svg.aria-label: Anatomy of a 240-byte GhostMesh frame: what each field does, how it protects confidentiality, integrity and availability, and what Meshtastic's cleartext header leaks by comparison.
svg.text: Anatomy of a GhostMesh frame: 240 bytes, every frame the same size
What each byte does, how it keeps messages confidential, intact and deliverable, and why a sniffer learns so little. Offsets from PROTOCOL.md §9.4–9.5.
2 The 30-byte header, zoomed: the only part anyone can read
type: DATA, HELLO, CTRL or KEYS; ACKs travel as DATA
flags: only an SOS bit, no needs-ACK bit
Visible: the frame's class and SOS. Bound to the AEAD
Hop padding: the sender starts at hop 0, 1 or 2
ttl + hop is always 5, so hop 0 ≠ the sender
Always 0 = flood: no route, no destination
Every node tries to decrypt every frame;
Keyed BLAKE2b (network key) over all other 232 bytes
Checked first: outsiders' frames die at hop 1
Re-made by each relay; constant-time compare
Duplicate + replay caches (60 s and 180 s)
Bound to the AEAD: can't be swapped
Who TRANSMITTED (last hop), not who wrote it
Rotates every 60 s, with the radio MAC
Each relay overwrites it with its own
Only ±1 epoch is accepted: replays expire
Bound to the AEAD: can't be re-dated
3 The encrypted part: only the sender and the recipient can open it (not to scale)
Real sender + recipient, send time, sequence number,
real type (DATA or ACK) and length
Recipient checks: for me? from that peer? fresh (5 s)?
Padded so every frame is 240 B: length never leaks
Key: per pair of nodes, re-keyed every epoch
Seals the ciphertext AND type, flags,
One bit changed → the recipient drops it
4 The same job in Meshtastic: a 16-byte header that is never encrypted
Layout from meshtastic.org/docs/overview/mesh-algo and /encryption. Red: what a sniffer learns. Green: GhostMesh's answer.
payload: AES, length varies with the message
up to 239 B, unused bytes not sent
Leaks who talks to whom, every packet
IDs are fixed (CRC-32 of the node's key)
GhostMesh: no destination field; the sender
is a 60 s pseudonym of the last hop
Hops travelled = hop start − hop limit:
how far you are from the sender
GhostMesh: hop padding hides the start;
A key hint and relay IDs in the clear
Length follows the message; the default
Outside the 240 bytes: the radio MAC also changes every 60 s, together with src_pseudo.
